jobs.title: Retail & Used Car De-Fleet Manager - Europe
jobs.description:
About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

The Retail & Used Car De-Fleet Manager (Europe) is responsible for leading the end-to-end strategy and operations for vehicle de-fleeting, trade-in management, refurbishment, and sales across the European region.

This role is accountable for maximizing vehicle residual values through accurate valuation, effective refurbishment planning, efficient inventory management, and optimized route-to-market decisions. Working cross-functionally with Sales, Fleet, Service, Finance, and Retail Operations teams, the De-Fleet Manager ensures all returned and traded vehicles are processed efficiently, marketed through the most appropriate sales channels, and sold in a manner that maximizes profitability while supporting Lucid’s premium brand standards and customer experience.

The successful candidate will drive operational excellence, establish scalable de-fleet processes, develop strategic remarketing partnerships, and deliver performance through robust KPI management, ensuring a best-in-class used vehicle and Certified Pre-Owned operation across Europe.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead the valuation, pricing, and resale strategy for all Lucid trade-in and de-fleet vehicles, ensuring accurate vehicle appraisals, margin optimization, and effective route-to-market decisions.

• Develop and manage European used vehicle sales channels, including retail, wholesale, auction, and third-party marketplace partnerships, to maximize profitability, speed of sale, and market coverage.

• Design and oversee a standardized EU de-fleet process covering vehicle returns, inspections, refurbishment, logistics, storage, and sales readiness.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Service, Retail Operations, Fleet, and Finance teams to ensure efficient vehicle processing and minimize cost leakage.

• Define, track, and report key performance indicators related to vehicle turnaround times, refurbishment efficiency, inventory aging, channel performance, and profitability.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency, stock turn, customer experience, and financial performance.

• Support the implementation and ongoing management of the Certified Pre-Owned (CPO) program, ensuring vehicles meet brand, quality, and compliance standards.

• Manage fleet return processes with leasing and fleet partners, ensuring timely execution, accurate condition assessments, and maximum value recovery from returned vehicles.

• Identify and resolve process bottlenecks across the used vehicle lifecycle to improve operational performance and optimize residual value outcomes.

• Deliver a premium, end-to-end customer experience, guiding customers through every stage of the sales journey with a consultative approach, tailored solutions, and seamless vehicle delivery and ownership transition.

• Build lasting customer relationships and drive brand loyalty by proactively resolving issues, exceeding expectations, and continuously enhancing the customer experience to generate advocacy and satisfaction.

• Set up & drive campaigns (GTM) for all regions, in conjunction with the NSCs in relevant markets

Qualifications

• Experience in Automotive Management, Supply Chain, Finance, or a related discipline preferred, but not essential.

• Minimum of 8 years’ proven success in vehicle de-fleet, remarketing, used vehicle operations, or a related automotive industry role.

• Demonstrated expertise in end-to-end de-fleet and remarketing operations, including vehicle valuation, refurbishment planning and inventory management.

• Strong understanding of residual value management and the commercial drivers impacting profitability across wholesale and auction channels.

• Proven experience defining, managing, and reporting on key operational and financial KPIs within a de-fleet/remarketing environment.

• Proficient in CRM and business management systems, with Salesforce experience preferred.

• Excellent negotiation, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and build effective relationships with internal and external partners.

• Strong commercial acumen with a strategic mindset, capable of identifying growth opportunities, driving process improvements, and delivering sustainable business results.

• Highly analytical, results-oriented, and self-motivated, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Demonstrated ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams and international markets.

• Fluent in English, both written and spoken; additional European languages are advantageous.

This is a Lucid office-based role in Amsterdam

Compensation & Benefits: Lucid offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance; life and disability coverage; paid time off; paid holidays, paid sick leave; and a 401(k) retirement plan. Hourly/non-exempt employees accrue up to 120 hours paid time off, and salaried/exempt employee accrue up to 160 hours paid time off.  Eligible employees may also participate in Lucid’s equity program and/or a discretionary annual cash incentive program. Incentive and equity awards, if applicable, are determined based on individual performance, role scope, market considerations, and overall company results, in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.

Equal Opportunity: At Lucid, we believe diversity strengthens everything we build. Lucid Motors is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing an inclusive workplace for all. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national or ethnic origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable state or federal laws and regulations.

Accessibility: Lucid Motors is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need any accommodation to participate in the application process, please contact us at TA-Operations <@> lucidmotors.com. This email address is designated solely for accommodation requests and is not monitored for job applications or resume submissions. To be considered for employment, all applications must be submitted through the Lucid Motors Careers website.

Candidate Data Privacy: By submitting your application, you understand and agree that your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Notice.

To all recruitment agencies: Lucid Motors does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Lucid Motors. Lucid Motors is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Partner II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

SENIOR TALENT ACQUISITION PARTNER I

Based onsite between Rocket Lab’s Chantilly, VA and Wallops Island, VA site, the Senior Talent Acquisition Partner II is responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships with hiring managers and candidates alike to fill highly critical roles.

This is a full life-cycle recruitment position – you will own everything from initial sourcing and screening to extending offers. As a senior member of the TA team, you will be integral in fulfilling our mission to open up access to space to improve life on earth by hiring innovators who will help shape our rapidly expanding programs.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Serve as a strategic hiring expert and partner to hiring managers and business unit leaders

• Partner with hiring managers to determine the requirements and expectations for their open positions, and the qualities of their ideal candidate

• Manage the full hiring life-cycle, from initial sourcing and screening to extending offers

• Screen candidates for open roles and guide them through the interview process

• Build a diverse pipeline of talent, including passive candidates, through sourcing, cold calling, phone screens, and networking

• Utilize our ATS (Greenhouse) to build reports and analyze key metrics on recruiting activities to drive process improvements

• Travel as needed to support hiring efforts at our Launch Complex 3 site in Wallops Island VA.

YOU'LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor’s degree

• 8+ years of full-time recruiting experience

• 2+ years of recruiting experience in the aerospace industry.

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• 10+ years of full-time recruiting experience preferred

• Agency and in-house recruiting experience

• Experience recruiting for high-volume nonexempt roles and/or engineering roles such as: production, manufacturing, test, mechanical, electrical, systems, propulsion, etc.

• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment supporting high-performing teams

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate with hiring managers at all levels, as well as candidates and external partners

• Previous experience sourcing for highly technical and niche roles

This position may require prolonged periods of sitting, standing, walking, computer work, and occasional exposure to moderate levels of noise, dust, and fumes in production areas.

The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the state of Virginia’s pay transparency requirements. Final agreed upon compensation is based upon individual qualifications and experience.

Base salary is only one part of Rocket Lab’s compensation package for this role. You may be eligible for company stock, or cash incentives, and can purchase discounted stock through Rocket Lab’s Employee Stock Purchase Program. Employee benefits also include medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage; 401(k) retirement plan options; paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave; paid parental leave; and other discounts and perks.

Base Pay Range (VA Only)

$120,000—$155,000 USD

WHAT TO EXPECT

We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.

Important information:

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here.

Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.

FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:

For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality.  For more information on these Regulations, click here ITAR Regulations.

jobs.title: Sr. Product Marketing Manager, Government
jobs.description:
Product Marketing turns Chainalysis innovation into customer value. We position our intelligence as solutions customers can understand and consume through our platform, shape how we commercialize them, and give GTM the stories and strategic assets to win.


The public sector is a priority growth segment for Chainalysis, spanning law enforcement, intelligence agencies, regulators and tax authorities. As digital assets become more integrated into the financial system, these organizations need the intelligence, tools and tradecraft to advance their missions—from shaping policy and enforcing the rules to disrupting illicit networks and protecting national security. This role connects Chainalysis capabilities to those mission priorities, with a clear, compelling story for agency leaders and operational teams.



As Senior Product Marketing Manager for the Public Sector, you will own how Chainalysis shows up in the market for these buyers. You will shape our intelligence, data, products, AI capabilities, and services into a differentiated customer story—one that connects to real workflows, urgent problems, and mission outcomes.


This is a role for a strong marketer and an exceptional writer. You can take a complex capability, a shifting market, or a fuzzy customer problem and shape it into a sharp point of view, a persuasive narrative, and practical tools that sellers and customers actually use. You will work closely with Product, Sales, Marketing & Communications, subject-matter experts, and GTM Solutions & Readiness teams to make the story land in the market.



In this role, you’ll:

Position the value

 - Define and evolve the public sector value narrative: what Chainalysis enables, why it matters, and why we are meaningfully different.

 - Build messaging for priority buyer and user personas, from agency leaders to investigators, intelligence analysts, regulators and tax specialists.

 - Create the narratives, proof points, and strategic assets that help sellers communicate differentiated value with conviction.

 - Own public-sector competitive intelligence, translating market moves into clear offensive and defensive positioning for deal teams.



Turn value into solutions

 - Partner with Product, R&D, Marketing & Communications, and subject-matter experts to translate innovation into compelling industry solutions, use cases, and sales plays.

 - Lead go-to-market planning for launches, major releases, platform capabilities, and commercial offerings.

 - Shape customer-facing value narratives for pricing, packaging, and usage-based commercial models, including business cases, operational value and mission impact.

 - Bring a customer lens to product and market decisions: explain not only what a capability does, but how it advances the customer’s mission.



Win and learn in market

 - Produce the strategic content that moves government opportunities forward: first-call decks, solution briefs, talk tracks, discovery frameworks, proof points, and sales plays.

 - Partner with Product, Product Marketing, GTM & Enablement teams to scale the strongest narratives into field tools and enablement.

 - Bring customer, field, partner, and competitive insight back into the work — sharpening positioning, converting market evidence into credible stories, and building repeatable use cases.



We’re looking for candidates who have: 


 - 5–8 years in product, solutions, industry, or B2B enterprise technology marketing, with experience marketing to public-sector customers across law enforcement, intelligence, regulatory or tax functions.

 - A demonstrated ability to build positioning and messaging that changes how customers and sellers see a problem—not simply content that fills a library.

 - Exceptional writing and editorial judgment. You can write crisp headlines, persuasive narratives, practical sales content, and executive-level messaging; you know the difference between jargon and precision.

 - Strong understanding of public-sector buying journeys, decision-making processes and mission-oriented sales motions.

 - The ability to connect technical capabilities to mission and operational value for both executive buyers and hands-on users.

 - A collaborative self-starter, comfortable working across R&D, Sales, technical and revenue teams, and senior leaders to drive ambiguous, multi-stakeholder work forward independently.



Nice to have experience:

 - Experience with blockchain, digital assets, or crypto-native financial infrastructure.

 - Experience marketing AI-powered products, data platforms, intelligence products, cybersecurity, or risk and compliance technology.

 - Familiarity with consumption- or usage-based pricing and packaging.

 - Familiarity with investigative, intelligence, national-security, regulatory or tax use cases for intelligence and technology, and the policy developments shaping digital-asset markets.



You’ll thrive here if:

You can shape complexity into a story people remember and a sales conversation people can use. You write with precision, bring sound judgment to ambiguous problems, build for repeatability rather than one-off requests, and care about the quality of what reaches customers and the field.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.



About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.



You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

jobs.title: Electrical Architect, Body Systems Lead
jobs.location: Novi, Michigan, United States; Charlotte, North Carolina, United States
jobs.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Overview

Electrical Architect, Body Systems Lead is responsible for defining and managing the electrical and electronic architecture for Body Systems and for leading integration across related vehicle functions. This role bridges systems engineering, software development, electrical hardware, and cross-functional coordination to ensure functional integration and compliance with vehicle-level requirements. As the lead architect for the assigned Body Systems scope, this position addresses significant and unique technical issues, exercises independent judgment, and drives architecture decisions that may impact the broader function.

What you’ll do

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

Body Systems Architecture Execution

Define the advanced electrical architecture for Body Systems applications and develop the associated vehicle architecture data process. Evaluate complex interdependencies and technical tradeoffs across functional, logical, and physical architectures; identify inconsistencies; and devise solutions where precedent or complete information may not exist. Lead architecture alignment with Main System architects and related domains, and ensure consistency with vehicle-level requirements. Coordinate across groups, convey advanced technical information, and persuade diverse stakeholders to reach architecture decisions.

Body Systems Functions and Integration Leadership

Own system architecture and integration for assigned Body Systems functions from concept through production and post-launch support. Provide technical direction across relevant electrical, software, mechanical, controls, and validation interfaces; arbitrate cross-domain technical issues; and guide teams toward solutions that support overall vehicle and functional objectives. Act as a recognized subject matter expert for the assigned Body Systems architecture scope.

Project Timeline for Body Systems Development

Lead the architecture, integration, and validation readiness of assigned Body Systems functions in accordance with program timing. Drive functional deliverables to agreed milestones, including prototype builds, design verification (VFF), product validation (PVS), and vehicle launch gates. Evaluate risks and intangibles that may affect functional or program success, establish technical recovery direction when needed, and ensure required software, hardware, interface, and test deliverables are decision-ready at each milestone.

Roles and Responsibilities

• Own end-to-end electrical and electronic architecture for assigned Body Systems scope and ensure alignment to vehicle-level architecture and program objectives.

• Lead development of functional, logical, and physical EE architecture with system engineers and domain experts, including resolution of significant and unique cross-domain issues.

• Define system-level requirements spanning EE, software, and mechanical interfaces and lead architecture design and integration at system and component levels. Serve as the technical liaison among hardware, applications, Body Systems teams, and core cross-functional teams.

• Lead end-to-end delivery and architecture readiness of key Body Systems functions against program milestones; exercise independent judgment in resolving ambiguous issues and technical tradeoffs.

• Coordinate across engineering and business groups throughout the system V-development lifecycle from concept through launch, leading technical alignment in design reviews and cross-functional forums and persuading diverse stakeholders when tradeoffs are required.

• Own functional and non-functional architecture requirements, development alignment, validation readiness, and technical architecture decisions for assigned Body Systems scope.

• Apply broad expertise in software controls, electrical/electronic systems, and mechatronics development, testing, and validation methods to guide cross-domain solutions.

• Lead development of component and system design inputs, functional and EOL specifications, detailed test methods, and system-level DFMEA, DV, and PV deliverables for complex mechatronic systems; guide application of established principles and development of new technical approaches when needed.

• Analytical development using model-based design, MBSE/MBD simulation toolsets, MIL/SIL/HIL

• Tool landscape familiar with JIRA, Confluence, Codebeamer, Preevision, CAMEO, Github, JFROG etc.

Location & Travel Expectations:

• This role will be based out of the Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC or Novi, Michigan.

• This role requires 4-5 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.

• Applicants should expect that the role will require the ability to convene with Scout colleagues in person and travel to participate in events on behalf of the company from time to time.

What you’ll bring

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You’ll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You’ll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

• Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field, with 12–15 years of relevant experience; equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered.

• Extensive automotive systems or mechatronics product experience, including Body Systems and cross-domain vehicle integration.

• Strong first-principles engineering capability with demonstrated ability to evaluate significant and unique technical issues and drive results.

• Recognized subject matter expertise in systems engineering, multi-domain physics, and complex system design involving electrical and software integration.

• Familiarity with SW for embedded systems, EE systems such as wiring and power distribution units.

• Familiarity with CAN, Automotive Ethernet, LIN, LVDS communication protocols and Vehicle Network tools, such as CANalyzer, CANoe, etc.

• Expertise in complex problem solving and data analysis, with demonstrated ability to influence diverse stakeholders, make sound independent technical judgments, and drive results across extended teams.

What you'll gain

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up.  This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation.  In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

• Competitive insurance including: Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans

• 401(k) program with: An employer match and immediate vesting

• Generous Paid Time Off including: 20 days planned PTO, as accrued 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave

Pay Transparency

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $160,000.00 - $192,500.00

Internal leveling code: IC7

Notice to applicants:

• To be considered for career opportunities at Scout Motors, applicants must be 18 years of age or older.

• Residing in San Francisco: Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

• Residing in Los Angeles: Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

• Residing in New York City: This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.

Equal Opportunity

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

jobs.title: AI-Led Scaled Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
TL;DR
This is a senior hybrid role, half building the scaled programs engine, half account ownership. You'll own a cohort of scaled customers directly, running their onboarding, driving adoption, and retaining them, while designing the scaled enablement programs, curricula, webinars, onboarding journeys, and lifecycle communications, that teach an entire customer base how to build with Lovable.

Your book of accounts is a test bed and a live classroom. What you prove there becomes the playbook for the whole CS organization. This role suits a past CSM ready to multiply their impact through scaled education, content, and automation, owning revenue outcomes like a CSM while building like a program leader.

Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we're just getting started.

We're building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe's fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What you'll do

Scaled programs (~50%)

 - Own post-purchase lifecycle communications and customer education across every channel and segment: email, in-app guides, Slack, release comms, and re-engagement plays

 - Architect Lovable's customer education academy, defining learning paths, designing the curricula and content (courses, video, labs, certification-ready material), and owning the roadmap from first course to a full academy

 - Build and host live education, including onboarding sessions, workshops, and feature deep-dives, turning recordings into an on-demand library

 - Design the digital onboarding journey for scaled customers, with sequenced comms, in-app guidance, and self-serve resources anchored to the learning paths

 - Package content into repeatable formats CSMs can deliver in their own accounts

 - Instrument everything to tie education and program performance to retention

Customer ownership (~50%)

 - Own a book of ~100s scaled-segment accounts end to end: run a disciplined renewal motion and manage risk early through direct engagement and automated plays, monitoring account health along the way, with most accounts self-served through your programs and your time reserved for moments of risk and opportunity

 - Guide customers from first project to load-bearing app, helping admins deploy the platform well and helping builders ship applications their teams depend on

 - Partner with Support to triage customer questions, keeping your time focused on proactive, high-leverage work

 - Surface product blockers, expansion signals, and success stories to Product, Sales, and Marketing, capturing the voice of the customer

How we'll measure success
 Scaled CS runs on the same core metrics as the rest of the team, no separate scoreboard.

 - Gross retention (DRR/GRR) on your book, the north star for the segment

 - Net active builders and net load-bearing apps, the impact of your programs across all accounts

 - Education metrics: learning-path completion, live session engagement, and time-to-first-value for educated vs. non-educated cohorts

 - Program metrics: onboarding completion, comms performance, and re-engagement conversion

 - Leverage metrics: motions from your book that graduate to team-wide adoption

What we're looking for

 - 6-8+ years in Scaled Success, customer success, customer education, or post-sales roles, with direct ownership of renewals and a track record of strong retention

 - Deep experience designing and delivering one-to-many programs at scale: curricula, learning paths or academies, webinars, digital onboarding, lifecycle email, or community, spanning both instructor-led and self-serve formats

 - A builder's instinct: comfortable prototyping with modern tools including Lovable itself, automating your own workflows, and using AI to extend your reach

 - Strong written and presentation skills, sharp enough to write an email sequence that converts and hold a room of 200 customers

 - Data fluency: you form hypotheses, instrument the programs to test them, and let results decide what scales

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship, this segment is being built and you'll help define how it works

 - Bonus: experience in a consumption/credit-based pricing model, PLG-to-enterprise motion, or developer/builder-adjacent products

jobs.title: UTM Engineer - DoorDash Air
jobs.description:
About the Team

The DoorDash Air team is bringing drone delivery to reality. To make this happen, we’re building a strong electrical team to design high reliability, high power density converters, and fault-tolerant controls electronics. Come join us to build a new class of aircrafts and deploy at scale.

DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better.

About the Role

We're hiring a Senior UTM Engineer who will build core components of DoorDash Air's internal route planning and airspace deconfliction stack — the systems that decide where our aircraft can safely fly, coordinate that with other operators and airspace authorities, and keep our internal stakeholders and external systems talking to each other in terms they understand. This is a role for someone who has already lived through the full lifecycle of a distributed, interoperable, uptime-critical system in a field where getting it wrong has real consequences — aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or similar — and wants to bring that judgment to a fast-moving aerial delivery network.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Design, build, and deploy interoperable services that must pass rigorous, often open-source, conformance and integration testing against external systems and partners.

• Develop novel path planning and airspace deconfliction algorithms that find safe, efficient routes through real-world, dynamic environments.

• Build tools that help our teams and systems evaluate and optimize airspace efficiency and utilization.

• Design integrations that connect the deconfliction stack to existing DoorDash systems, translating mission and airspace status into terms internal stakeholders can act on.

• Collaborate closely with systems engineering, commercial operations, and flight operations to ship features that hold up in real-world flight.

• Represent DoorDash Air externally — engaging with peer companies, working groups, and standards bodies to improve interoperable deployments industry-wide and help shape the

We’re excited about you because…

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

• You have 5+ years of experience across the full lifecycle — design, build, deployment, and operation — of distributed systems in aviation, finance, communications, healthcare, or another field where interoperability, uptime, and (ideally) safety criticality are core drivers of the work.

• You've built and shipped production services that had to interoperate with systems you didn't control, including passing external or open-source conformance/certification testing.

• You have hands-on experience with path planning, routing, or deconfliction problems in real-world, dynamic environments — or the algorithmic depth to pick this up quickly (graph search, optimization, or motion planning fundamentals).

• You're comfortable building evaluation and analysis tooling, not just the systems being evaluated — you like giving other teams visibility into system performance and efficiency.

• You can design clean integrations across organizational boundaries and translate technical system state into language that commercial, operations, and non-engineering stakeholders understand.

• You communicate well with non-technical stakeholders and are comfortable representing your work and your company outside of it — in standards working groups, industry forums, or direct collaboration with peers at other companies.

• You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with the languages and paradigms common to safety- and uptime-critical distributed systems (e.g., C++, Python, Go, or similar, plus familiarity with real-time or fault-tolerant system design).

• BS/MS/PhD in CS, EE, Aerospace, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have:

jobs.title: Director, Clinical Sciences
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Tango Therapeutics is a biotechnology company dedicated to discovering novel drug targets and delivering the next generation of precision medicine for the treatment of cancer.

Using an approach that starts and ends with patients, Tango leverages the genetic principle of synthetic lethality to discover and develop therapies that take aim at critical targets in cancer.

This includes expanding the universe of precision oncology targets into novel areas such as tumor suppressor gene loss and their contribution to the ability of cancer cells to evade immune cell killing.

Tango is located at 201 Brookline Avenue, in the vibrant Fenway area of Boston, Massachusetts.

Summary

Tango has an exciting opportunity to join the team as our Director, Clinical Sciences. This is a hands-on role with scientific contributions to one or more clinical development programs. The successful candidate will actively engage in the design, execution, analysis, and interpretation of clinical studies. You will ensure scientific rigor throughout study conduct, lead data review and analysis, and partner cross-functionally to advance clinical development programs. This role reports to the Executive Director, Clinical Sciences.

Your Role:

• Scientific contribution to one or more clinical programs to ensure the successful design, execution, and interpretation of clinical studies

• Provide scientific leadership throughout the design, execution, analysis, and interpretation of early- and late-stage oncology clinical trials

• Partner closely with Clinical Development physicians, Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacovigilance, Regulatory Affairs, Translational Medicine, and Medical Writing to ensure high-quality execution of clinical programs

• Contribute to the development and review of key clinical documents, including protocols, investigator brochures, informed consent forms, clinical study reports, clinical development plans, and regulatory briefing materials

• Interpret emerging clinical, safety, PK/PD, and biomarker data to inform study conduct, dose selection, expansion opportunities, and overall development strategy

• Contribute scientific expertise to regulatory submissions and health authority interactions

• Foster a collaborative, accountable, and scientifically rigorous culture within the Clinical Science function

• Perform additional duties and responsibilities as required

What You Bring:

• MD, PhD, PharmD, MS within a relevant scientific discipline

• At least 10 years of experience in clinical science, or research

• At least 5 years of experience in oncology

• Demonstrated experience in designing and managing clinical trials, including knowledge of regulatory guidelines and GCP

• Strong analytical skills with proficiency in statistical analysis and interpretation of clinical data

• Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to convey complex scientific concepts to diverse audiences

• Experience working in a fast-paced environment

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Salary range

$190,400—$285,600 USD

jobs.title: Student Life Senior Associate
jobs.description:
ABOUT ALU

At the African Leadership University (ALU), we are more than an academic institution; we are a launchpad for Africa’s next generation of leaders. Our mission is bold: to develop ethical, entrepreneurial changemakers who will shape Africa’s future. Through an innovative curriculum, hands-on learning, and a vibrant pan-African community, we equip our students to tackle complex challenges, connect the dots across diverse perspectives, and create solutions that drive lasting impact. We don’t just teach; we nurture adaptable, globally minded problem-solvers ready to thrive in ambiguity, build from scratch, and lead Africa into a prosperous 21st century.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Student Life team shapes students' lived experience beyond the classroom. We design the systems, programs, and support structures that ensure students feel safe, seen, and supported throughout their journey at ALU. From residential life and community culture to scholar support and wellbeing coordination, our work sits at the heart of campus life. We are a highly collaborative, student-centred team that balances empathy with structure. Our work requires a strong partnership across operations, wellness, academics, and external stakeholders. We care deeply about building inclusive communities, developing student leaders, and creating environments where students can thrive socially, personally, and academically.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Student Life Senior Associate plays a key operational and relational leadership role in delivering a safe, engaging, and well-coordinated campus life experience. This role is responsible for translating Student Life strategy into daily practice across residential experience, community engagement, and scholar financial aid support. As the primary operational lead supporting these areas, the Senior Associate designs and improves processes, manages student interns who support frontline operations, and ensures that systems, communications, and services are consistent, student-centred, and policy-aligned. The role works across teams to strengthen campus culture, uphold student wellbeing, and ensure smooth service delivery throughout the student journey. In emergencies and sensitive situations, the Senior Associate serves as a secondary responder, supporting crisis coordination and safeguarding processes under the guidance of the Student Life Manager.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Residential Experience & Campus Living Operations

• Lead day-to-day residential life operations, ensuring a safe, structured, and community-oriented living environment

• Coordinate student arrivals, transitions, and residential logistics for both local and international students

• Design and implement residential programming that fosters belonging, leadership, and healthy community culture

• Support crisis response in residences as a secondary responder, ensuring proper escalation, documentation, and follow-through

• Work closely with security, wellness, and operations teams to uphold student safety and well-being

• Draft, update, and implement residential life policies, guidelines, and standard operating procedures

• Manage relationships with key residential vendors (e.g. catering, transport, medical) and ensure service quality and accountability

• Oversee residential life budgets and support financial tracking and documentation

2. Student Leadership & Community Engagement

• Design and support training and development programs for student leaders (e.g. Residential Advisors, peer leaders, community coordinators)

• Create leadership structures and engagement opportunities that strengthen student ownership of campus life

• Partner with student governance bodies to ensure strong collaboration between student leaders and staff

• Support major campus moments such as orientation, community celebrations, and institutional events

• Lead feedback collection and community listening processes to continuously improve student experience initiatives

3. Financial Aid & Scholar Support

• Serve as a key point of contact for scholarship students, providing ongoing communication and guidance

• Support scholarship onboarding, orientation, and financial literacy initiatives

• Coordinate scholar travel logistics, documentation support, and arrival processes

• Prepare and process documentation required for scholarship disbursements in partnership with Finance and Registrar teams

• Support students facing financial difficulty through structured processes and referrals

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to monitor scholar wellbeing, integration, and overall experience

• Support engagement initiatives that strengthen scholar community and belonging

4. Intern Leadership & Frontline Operations

• Supervise and mentor student interns supporting Residential Life, Residential Operations, and Financial Aid

• Provide structured onboarding, task management, and professional development for interns

• Ensure interns are well-trained, supported, and operating within clear boundaries and expectations

• Coordinate intern schedules and responsibilities to ensure smooth frontline service delivery across student life functions

5. Operations, Data & Process Excellence

• Design and improve operational processes, ensuring they are efficient, student-centred, and aligned with institutional policies (with approval from the Student Life Manager)

• Maintain accurate and up-to-date student life data systems and trackers to support decision-making and reporting

• Manage Student Life communication channels, ensuring timely and clear communication with students and stakeholders

• Support reporting, documentation, and compliance processes related to residential life and scholar support

• Contribute to periodic reviews of policies and processes to improve service quality and risk management

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

• A relevant university degree

• Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in student affairs, residential life, community engagement, financial aid support, or a related student-facing operational role

• Demonstrated experience managing programs or services that support student wellbeing and community life

• Experience supervising, mentoring, or coordinating student staff, interns, or volunteers

• Proven ability to design or improve operational processes and manage multiple workstreams simultaneously

• Experience working with sensitive student information and navigating complex or confidential situations with professionalism

REQUIRED COMPETENCIES

Functional Competencies

• Manage complex operations with strong planning, prioritisation, and follow-through

• Design and improve processes that balance student experience with policy and compliance

• Use data systems and digital tools effectively to track operations and inform decisions

• Communicate clearly and professionally with diverse stakeholders, including students, staff, and external partners

• Coordinate crisis or sensitive situations with composure, documentation, and appropriate escalation

Behavioural & Leadership Competencies

• Builds strong, trust-based relationships with students while maintaining clear professional boundaries

• Demonstrates high empathy paired with sound judgment and policy alignment

• Engages actively in community-building and fosters inclusive environments

• Remains calm, solutions-oriented, and steady during periods of stress or ambiguity

• Exercises assertiveness in upholding standards, processes, and expectations

• Works collaboratively across teams and is open to feedback and continuous improvement

jobs.title: Director of Business Operations and Systems
jobs.description:
We are seeking a talented individual to join our team as a Director of Business Operations and Systems.

In this role, you will be at the forefront of optimizing our revenue and business systems ecosystem - spanning Sales, Customer Success, Account Management, Implementation, and Deal Desk. Reporting to the SVP - Operations, you will act as a strategic systems architect, RevOps partner, and team lead managing 2 direct reports

You will bridge high-level strategy and hands-on execution: architecting system flows, managing Nue CPQ, driving forecasting and pipeline reporting, and leading day-to-day systems operations while mentoring your team.

WHO YOU ARE

RevOps Partnership & Revenue Strategy

• Strategic Business Partner: Trusted operational partner to Sales, Marketing, Finance and Customer Success leaders for process optimization, territory/capacity insights, pipeline reviews, and GTM execution.

• Forecasting & Revenue Analytics: Skilled in building and maintaining revenue metrics, renewal forecasting, NRR/GRR tracking, and churn analysis to identify systemic revenue risks.

• Process Architecture: Experienced in mapping pre- and post-sale customer journeys, handoffs, and operational playbooks to drive retention, expansion, and team efficiency.

Systems Architecture & Tech Stack Governance

• Salesforce & CPQ Ownership: Hands-on architect and administrator for Salesforce (system of record) and Nue CPQ, owning product catalogs, SKU/packaging creation, pricebooks, custom attribute setups, and Deal Desk approvals.

• End-to-End System Integration: Expert in designing scalable data flows across interconnected GTM tools (Planhat, LeanData, Maxio, Outreach, Highspot, ChiliPiper) with minimal manual overhead.

• Data Architecture & Governance: Skilled in creating technical documentation, field libraries, change logs, and data quality standards that keep cross-system data accurate and audit-ready.

Team Leadership & Project Management

• Player-Coach & Team Lead: Proven ability to lead a small team—managing sprint intake, setting clear priorities, conducting flow/code reviews, and developing technical capacity.

• Project Delivery: Experienced in leading complex system implementations from requirements gathering through vendor evaluation, testing, deployment, and change management.

• Practical AI & Automation: Skilled in leveraging modern AI and automation tools to streamline workflows, enrich CRM data, and improve operational output.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

RevOps Leadership & Business Partnership

• Act as the primary operational partner for Sales, Marketing, Finance and CS leadership—translating business priorities into actionable revenue strategies and system workflows.

• Own revenue operations, including renewal/expansion forecasting, weekly pipeline hygiene, NRR channel updates, and churn analysis.

• Manage Deal Desk operational reviews, order form templates, custom SKU controls, and monthly Finance reconciliations (SFDC Maxio) to maintain quote-to-cash alignment.

• Conduct quarterly pricing and discounting analysis in partnership with Finance and Product Marketing to evaluate historical trends and margin impact.

Systems Architecture & Administration

• Serve as primary architect and hands-on administrator for Salesforce and Nue CPQ, maintaining high system availability, flow logic, and data integrity.

• Co-own the business systems roadmap with the SVP of Operations driving structured intake, trade-off evaluations, and deployment release calendars.

• Manage the Planhat-to-Salesforce data flow, ensuring seamless bi-directional synchronization for customer health scores, renewal milestones, and usage data.

• Oversee user access provisioning, security configuration reviews, and license management across all GTM and revenue tools.

• Manage GTM system vendor contracts, renewals, invoice approvals, and systems budget allocations.

Team Management & Operations

• Lead, mentor, and direct small team

• Establish structured intake, prioritization, and sprint cadences for all RevOps and systems requests across the organization.

• Maintain comprehensive technical documentation, architecture maps, and user training guides for all system modifications.

• Perform other operational duties and special projects as assigned.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE / KEY MILESTONES

First 3 Months

• System Audit & CPQ Onboarding: Complete a comprehensive audit of the business systems landscape and successfully complete onboarding on Nue CPQ, taking full ownership of SKU management, pricebook updates, and Deal Desk approvals.

• Data Governance Framework: Establish and document data governance standards across Salesforce, Planhat, and Maxio, delivering a remediation plan for identified data quality issues.

• Process Alignment: Establish a recurring RevOps reporting cadence for post-sales leadership (NRR/churn analytics) and streamline the monthly SFDC Maxio reconciliation workflow.

• Targeted Operational Win: Achieve a measurable reduction in quote cycle time or CPQ order form error rate.

First 6 Months

• Automated Renewal & Expansion Workflow: Design and deploy a semi-automated renewal tracking process between Planhat and Salesforce with automated status triggers and clear checkpoint ownership.

• Roadmap Execution: Deliver at least three prioritized roadmap projects (e.g., LeanData routing optimization, CPQ structure cleanup, or automated attribution mapping).

• Quantifiable Efficiency Targets: Achieve measurable improvements across key metrics:

• Reduce custom SKU exception requests by 20% through standardized Nue CPQ rules.

• Improve Planhat-to-Salesforce data synchronization accuracy to

• Decrease lead routing turnaround times.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

• 6+ years of progressive experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or Business Systems within a B2B SaaS environment.

• 3+ years of team lead or managerial experience guiding direct reports (delegating sprint tasks, conducting technical reviews, and mentoring team members).

• Deep Salesforce Expertise: Advanced experience with Salesforce strategy, architecture, complex Flows, and system integration patterns.

• Hands-on CPQ Experience: Direct administration experience with CPQ platforms (Nue CPQ preferred).

• Post-Sales Tooling Knowledge: Hands-on experience administering Customer Success platforms (Planhat, Gainsight, ChurnZero, or similar) integrated with CRM systems.

• SaaS Revenue Metrics: Strong understanding of B2B SaaS financial models, including ARR, NRR, GRR, logo retention, quote-to-cash, and sales capacity modeling.

• Data & Analytics Rigor: Expert-level capability in reporting, dashboard creation, data modeling, and financial system reconciliations (e.g., SFDC to Maxio).

• Education: Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, Finance, or equivalent practical experience.

Post Sales Tools

• CRM & Core: Salesforce (Sales, Service, Experience Clouds)

• CPQ & Finance Billing: Nue CPQ, Maxio

• Customer Success & Engagement: Planhat, Intercom

• Marketing & Sales Engagement: Pardot, Outreach, ChiliPiper, LeanData

• Intelligence & Analytics: ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Chorus.ai, Gong, 6Sense, Highspot

• Collaboration: Slack, Teams, Zoom

LOCATION

We are a fully remote company! Rather than restrict ourselves to only finding talent in one city, we’d rather find the absolute best people regardless of where they live.

jobs.title: Social Creative Lead
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

Neko needs its social channels to keep moving while the Creative Studio team in Stockholm is offline. This role owns social creative for the US: it takes an editorial system of content pillars and turns it into work that is shot, edited and published, so the feed stays distinct and coherent (Impact, not activity). You work directly with Ramiro on the visual language and with Marketing on strategy, copy and the editorial calendar.




WHAT YOU’LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS

 - By month 3: a steady shoot, edit and publish rhythm across the agreed content categorization with every post traceable to a pillar and its toolbox.

 - By month 6: a platform playbook agreed with Marketing, setting out audience and format per category for Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn (Chase 10X, not 10%).

 - By month 9: content for a US location opening, shot on site with a videographer, from brief to published.

 - By month 12: a documented social framework and operating model that lets the function grow into a pod.

 - Easy to miss: US posts that ship overnight for Stockholm without a review from creative leadership, and a weekly read on platform and trend shifts that changes what the team makes.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own social creative for the US, from idea to published post.

 - Shoot and edit your own still and motion content, fast.

 - Run the editorial toolbox: apply each category look, tools and audience, and decide when to break it.

 - Draft captions and copy, with Marketing owning strategy, tent-pole moments and the calendar.

 - Direct freelance videographers and other external partners on location.

 - Track platform and algorithm shifts weekly, and say what you would change.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - A portfolio of social-first work you shot, edited and published yourself, still and motion, at a steady cadence.

 - Evidence of leading work end to end, from idea to shoot to published post, with outcomes you can state.

 - Evidence of working inside an editorial or design system, and knowing when to push against it.

 - Platform judgment for Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn, backed by a current view of trends.

 - Proven autonomy: making and owning calls without sign-off across a six-hour time difference.

 - US-based, and able to travel for one to two weeks on location.

 - Ability to leverage AI when appropriate; AI should speed up ideation, tagging, rough cuts and caption drafts, with a person checking quality and tone. It should not decide what is published, and it is not used for anything involving members’ health information or sign-off.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience directing a videographer, agency or freelancers.

 - Background at a direct-to-consumer, health, tech, and consumer goods.

 - Experience building a social framework or content design system, or supporting a location launch.


ABOUT TITLES AT NEKO

We use a simplified internal title framework that prioritises clarity over hierarchy, so internal titles may differ from market-facing role titles. Scope, impact and level of the role are fully aligned and will be clearly discussed throughout the process.




HIRING PROCESS

Candidates progress from application and structured screening through thoughtfully designed interviews, culminating in a formal offer and final pre-employment checks before joining the team.




EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & INCLUSION STATEMENT

Neko Health is committed to inclusive hiring and member-first care. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to request reasonable adjustments to support your application.

jobs.title: Director, Supplier Business Development (US) - NYC
jobs.description:
Location: Hybrid in Manhattan, New York, United States

Salary: Competitive base + Commission




ABOUT NIVODA 🚀

Nivoda is a global B2B diamond and gemstone marketplace that connects jewelry retailers with competitive, high-quality suppliers. With operations spanning multiple regions, Nivoda enables businesses to grow profitably by minimizing inventory risks and optimizing the supply chain. Our commitment to excellence, transparency, and innovation drives every part of our business — from supplier relationships to customer success.




OUR MISSION 🎯

Diamond and gemstone trading has long been plagued by inefficiency, opacity, and exclusivity. Nivoda was built to change that - to democratise access and empower every business, regardless of size or location, to buy and sell with confidence. Independent jewellers are at the heart of this mission. They deserve the same access to quality, pricing, and selection as the biggest players in the industry. That's exactly what we give them.




ABOUT THE ROLE 🤔

As our Director of Supplier Business Development, you’ll play a critical role in growing and managing our supplier base for our B2B diamond marketplace. This is a customer-facing, relationship-led role for a driven, strategic professional who excels in building trusted supplier partnerships both in person and remotely, optimizing supplier performance, and aligning their products with market demand.

You’ll act as a co-pilot and primary point of contact for suppliers - working closely with them from onboarding through sustained success. A key part of this role involves regular face-to-face meetings with existing and prospective suppliers, representing Nivoda locally and ensuring suppliers feel supported, informed, and set up to succeed. Your work will ensure our platform offers the best quality, selection, and value for buyers, creating a dynamic and profitable environment for both suppliers and our business.




WHAT WOULD YOU BE DOING? 😎

In this role, you’ll identify, onboard, and support high-potential suppliers while maximizing their sales growth and ensuring quality and inventory alignment with customer demand. You will act as both a consultant and a coach, guiding suppliers to optimize their product offerings, pricing, and availability. Through hands-on relationship management and on-the-ground presence in NYC, your insights and proactive support will be instrumental in helping suppliers grow on our platform and creating a seamless experience for buyers.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Supplier Acquisition and Onboarding:

 - Identify and onboard high-quality suppliers that align with category standards.

 - Conduct in-person and virtual meetings to communicate marketplace value propositions clearly and drive strong engagement with our platform.

Account Management and Supplier Support:

 - Build deep, consultative relationships with suppliers and serve as their day-to-day point of contact for growth, performance, and issue resolution.

 - Proactively support supplier needs, escalating and coordinating internally with tech, operations, and customer support teams to ensure a seamless experience.

Performance Analysis and Reporting:

 - Use data to assess supplier performance, identify growth opportunities, and provide actionable feedback on selection, pricing, availability, and quality metrics.

Sales Enablement and Revenue Growth:

 - Drive suppliers to meet revenue targets by optimizing product assortment, pricing strategies, and inventory levels. Promote express stock and fast-delivery initiatives to improve conversion and buyer satisfaction.

Quality and Compliance Oversight:

 - Work closely with suppliers to maintain high-quality standards, proactively reducing return rates and customer complaints through ongoing quality monitoring and guidance.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

 - Partner closely with category management, product, operations, and product marketing teams to align on category objectives, supplier priorities, and buyer engagement initiatives.

Supplier Training and Development:

 - Support the development and delivery of training resources to help suppliers adopt best practices for product listing optimization, quality control, and performance improvement.


WHAT DO WE NEED FROM YOU? 💪

 - 8+ years experience in sales, business development, or account management within the wholesale diamond or jewelry industry

 - Commercially sharp with a strategic mindset and experience negotiating with suppliers

 - Confident building relationships with business owners and decision-makers who are time-poor and sceptical of vendor sales pitches

 - Tech-savvy, with confidence in working with various digital tools day-to-day.

 - Self-starter mentality, you're the first on the ground, which means you'll need to operate with ambiguity, build your own structure, and create your own momentum

 - Data-driven approach to account management: you use CRM and platform data to prioritise your time and conversations

 - Excellent communicator - clear, direct, and credible with senior stakeholders and small business owners alike
   
   


NICE TO HAVE ✨

 - Familiarity with wholesale buying patterns, inventory-led businesses, or supply chain dynamics

 - Proven track record of driving revenue growth through partner or supplier relationships

 - Background at a high-growth marketplace or platform business with a strong enterprise or SMB sales culture

If you’re excited by a role that combines commercial impact, relationship ownership, and on-the-ground supplier engagement, we’d love to hear from you. This position is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-moving environment and enjoys being the trusted local partner suppliers rely on to grow their business.




OUR CULTURE AND WHAT WE OFFER 😉

At Nivoda, we believe that employees today want to evolve in a collaborative, high-growth environment where they can demonstrate their abilities and thrive both professionally and personally.

We are convinced that employees need to find alignment between their inner values and their company’s culture and mission to unlock their full potential. We work to create a culture of empowerment, continuous learning and growth where everyone can bring expertise, own projects and easily measure their impact. Dynamic working environment in a rapidly growing company. Enjoy a pleasant, low-hierarchy work environment. Engage in intellectually challenging work that contributes significantly to Nivoda’s success and scalability.




OUR CURRENT BENEFITS

🕰️ A vibrant company culture
🏥 Medical (United Healthcare), Dental, & Vision (Guardian Life) benefit

💸 401K benefit (Guideline Inc)
🧠 Plenty of opportunities for growth and learning
🏖️ Unlimited holiday allowance
🚀 Chance to join and contribute to a company during its exponential expansion phase

Nivoda is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to promoting diversity. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status.
Even if it seems you don't meet 100% of our musts don't let it stop you, we are all about finding the best talent out there! Skills can be learned, and embracing diversity is invaluable.

Please note: Our Talent Acquisition Team is international. We kindly ask you to please submit your CV and application in English so that it can be reviewed correctly.

*If after reading this job description you believe this is not the best fit for you, we’d encourage you to join our Talent Pool so we can keep you in mind as new roles open up.
You can sign up here: Nivoda Talent Pool https://nivoda.com/careers?ashby_jid=384ab7fa-bcf9-45ab-8665-f5ee26476804

This ensures you're among the first to hear about openings aligned with your skills and interests.

jobs.title: Structures Engineer II
jobs.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

Divergent aims to revolutionize industrial manufacturing in the aerospace and defense industries through our DAPS (Divergent Adaptive Production System) technology. Our patented production system incorporates Nodes™ – 3D-printed metal connectors – with lightweight materials to create strong and efficient complex structures. Divergent’s technology eliminates tooling and drives radical innovation, capital reduction, and sustainability in vehicle manufacturing.

Divergent is seeking a skilled and motivated engineer to support the next generation of industry-leading aerospace vehicle development. We’re committed to transforming vehicles’ structural systems away from traditional manufacturing by using new materials and new technologies.  To do this, we need a forward-looking and innovative engineer who will help shape the future of automotive structures.

As a Structures Engineer II, you will support structural engineering and product development activities across aerospace programs while contributing to design, analysis, and testing efforts.

The Role

• Create and maintain CAD models, FE models, and engineering documentation.

• Support structural analysis and validation activities.

• Assist with prototype builds, testing, and troubleshooting.

• Collaborate with manufacturing and design teams.

• Support engineering change implementation and product development efforts.

Basic Qualifications

• BS/MS in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.

• 3+ years of structural engineering experience.

• CAD experience; Siemens NX preferred.

• Familiarity with FEA tools and aerospace structures.

• Strong communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.

Work Environment

• Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboards.

Compensation

At Divergent, our pay range is based on the level of the job. For this role, we will consider candidates at levels E03 - E07 as evaluated through our interview process.

• Engineer / E03: $100,980 - $138,820

• Engineer II / E04: $116,600 - $160,325

• Senior Engineer / E05: $134,640 - $185,130

• Lead Engineer / E06: $155,540 - 213,840

• Principal Engineer / E07: $179,630 - 247,005

Pay Range

$100,980—$247,005 USD

What We Offer:

• Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

• Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

• Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

• Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.

• Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.
