jobs.title: VP of GRC
jobs.description:
WHY ZANIA

Every enterprise spends millions of dollars on Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). It's one of the most critical, yet universally painful, parts of running a business. For decades, this industry has been dominated by legacy systems with notoriously low NPS scores, making it totally ripe for disruption.

Zania is building agentic AI for Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) to solve this massive problem. We are on a rocketship trajectory, creating intelligent agents that automate and augment the most complex risk and compliance workflows. We have found exceptional product-market fit and are scaling our team very quickly. Some reasons to join Zania are:

 - Dream Customers: Our customers are the most notable enterprises in the world, including FAANG, Big 4 firms, and a portfolio of top customers.

 - Tier 1 Backing: Funded by a leading Tier 1 venture capital fund. Series A led by NEA, with Anthropic and Menlo Ventures. $18M raised to build a generational company.

 - World-Class Team: Zania is hiring the best. Our team includes AI and Security leaders from Airbnb, Microsoft, Bain & Company, Deloitte, PwC, Brex, and Instacart.

 - Hyper-Growth: We have seen 10x ARR growth in the last year and are rapidly expanding.

 - Competitive Compensation & Equity.


THE ROLE

As VP of GRC, you will build and lead Zania's customer-facing GRC organization. You will be the senior GRC voice in front of our largest customers and partners, turning Zania's agents into audit-ready outcomes across SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, NIST, HIPAA, PCI DSS, and third-party risk programs, delivered faster and with more coverage than any traditional team.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and Big 4 firms who are replacing weeks of manual compliance work with agents. You will own how those engagements are scoped, delivered, and expanded, and you will work with the founders, product, and AI engineering to make sure what we learn in the field makes our agents better.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build the GRC organization: Hire, coach, and scale a team of GRC leads, solutions architects, and compliance specialists.

 - Own customer delivery: Lead GRC engagements end to end, from scoping and onboarding through gap assessments, controls testing, audit readiness, and third-party risk programs.

 - Be the executive GRC advisor: Serve as a trusted advisor to CISOs, CROs, Chief Audit Executives, and Big 4 and advisory partners.

 - Build agent-first playbooks: Design repeatable delivery methodologies across SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, NIST CSF/800-53, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, DORA, and the EU AI Act.

 - Shape the product: Partner with product and AI engineering to turn field insight into agent capabilities, evaluation criteria, and human-in-the-loop guardrails.

 - Support strategic deals: Lead GRC discovery, solution design, and proof-of-value work with the sales team on our largest opportunities.

 - Measure what matters: Define and report on time to audit readiness, assessment cycle time, vendor coverage, customer satisfaction, and expansion.


REPRESENTATIVE PROJECTS

 - Take a Fortune 500 customer from kickoff to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 audit readiness in weeks using Zania's agents, and turn it into a repeatable playbook.

 - Roll out Zania Autonomous TPRM across a customer's full vendor base, moving coverage from a fraction of vendors to 100% of in-scope vendors.

 - Build an ISO 42001 and EU AI Act readiness offering with a Big 4 partner for enterprises adopting AI.


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Deep GRC expertise (required): You have run audits, assessments, and remediation programs yourself and can speak credibly with CISOs, auditors, and risk leaders about any major framework.

 - Customer-facing leadership: You have led client-facing GRC or audit teams and know how to deliver high-stakes engagements on time.

 - Executive presence: You build trust quickly with security, risk, and audit leaders at large enterprises and advisory firms.

 - Builder mentality: You have built a team, practice, or program from early stages and are comfortable owning it end to end.

 - AI curiosity: You believe agents will change how GRC work gets done and want to help define how.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Accounting, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 12+ years of experience in GRC, IT audit, or security compliance.

 - 5+ years leading customer-facing GRC, audit, or advisory teams.

 - Hands-on expertise with SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, and third-party risk management.

 - Strong structured written and verbal communication skills.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a Big 4 or advisory firm, or at a GRC platform company.

 - Certifications such as CISA, CISSP, CRISC, CISM, or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor.

 - Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act).

 - Experience as an early leader at a high-growth startup.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary + significant equity

 - Flexible PTO

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - Meals and snacks in the office

 - Relocation and immigration support

Zania is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law.

jobs.location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of endpoints across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time-sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kill chains and enable mission autonomy.

Within Connected Warfare, the Army portfolio encompasses some of the largest and most consequential programs in modern defense including NGC2 and TITAN. These programs sit at the intersection of mission command, fires, and intelligence—the operational convergence that is reshaping how the Army fights.

ABOUT THE JOB

Overview:
As the Army Growth Leader, you will own the growth strategy, customer relationships, and capture execution for Anduril’s Army mission command and C2 portfolio end-to-end. You will be responsible for maintaining the NGC2 scale plan, expanding TITAN, and positioning the company to apply Lattice as the Army’s Intelligence Data Layer.

This is a hands-on capture role, not a strategy-and-coordination position. You will personally shape requirements with PAE and CPE leadership, execute aggressive capture campaigns, and cultivate the customer relationships that turn Anduril from a program participant into an enduring platform owner. You must understand how intelligence feeds into fires and command workflows at an operational depth that commands immediate credibility with general officer and senior civilian leadership.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Own the Number: Carry full accountability for the Army growth plan, pipeline health, capture velocity, and multi-year revenue trajectory against the NGC2 scale plan

• Grow TITAN: Execute capture strategies to expand Anduril’s footprint across the Army, positioning Anduril’s mesh and data infrastructure to capture the AIDP Data Layer, bridging mission command and intelligence to establish Anduril as the core architecture provider moving sensor data to shooters

• Shape Requirements Upstream: Engage program executive offices, Army acquisition executives, and requirements owners 12–18 months in advance of solicitations to align requirements with Anduril’s edge compute, mesh networking, and software-defined C2 capabilities.

• Own Senior Army Relationships: Serve as the primary growth face to Army acquisition executives, operational commanders at the 1- and 2-star level, and key leadership across PAE C2, T2COM, and ASA(ALT).

• Lead Tier-1 Pursuits: Personally direct capture campaigns for 8- and 9-figure programs from early shaping through proposal submission and contract award, orchestrating engineering, product, pricing, and teaming strategies.

• Outmaneuver the competition: Track competitor positioning across major programs to identify vulnerabilities, assess where incumbents are entrenched, and structure plays to displace or dilute their market share.

• Drive Cross-Functional Alignment: Maintain tight feedback loops between customer requirements and internal product/engineering teams to ensure that what is sold can be built, delivered, and sustained at scale.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Active TS/SCI security clearance.

• 10+ years of experience in defense business development, capture, or growth leadership, with significant focus on Army C2, ISR, or intelligence domains.

• Deep operational fluency in the convergence of intelligence, fires, and mission command workflows, including sensor-to-shooter data pipelines and targeting architectures.

• In-depth understanding of the Army modern C2 landscape and shifting acquisition boundaries.

• Proven track record of directly shaping requirements at the PAE/PEO level that resulted in captured programs valued in the 8- to 9-figure range.

• Demonstrated success leading competitive captures that displaced or diluted entrenched defense incumbents.

• Robust, active network across PAE C2, T2COM, ASA(ALT), and operational units at the 1- and 2-star command levels.

• Hands-on capture leadership style with deep command of pricing models, teaming strategies, proposal development, and executive gate reviews.

• Experience leveraging rapid, non-traditional acquisition mechanisms (OTAs, middle-tier acquisitions) and integrating software-first solutions into defense hardware programs.

jobs.title: Partnerships Lead, New Verticals
jobs.description:
About Figure

Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.

Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies.

About the Role

You will scale three New Verticals: depository institutions, home improvement, and small business lending.

This role grows the volume of loans originated on Figure's platform. We want lenders, platforms, and depository institutions to originate on Figure's loan origination system, through private-label programs, embedded and SaaS-style integrations, and direct adoption. You take these partnerships from first conversation through launch and scaling: structuring the commercial terms, negotiating, and pulling together the internal teams needed to launch.

You will report to the Director of Platform Partnerships and primarily own the hard middle of the process, where partnerships are actually won or lost.

Work across Figure's key growth markets (including small business, home improvement, and depository institutions) to bring partners onto the platform via direct relationships, private-label programs, embedded integrations, and key channel ecosystem partnerships.

What You'll Do

• Map the market and source high-value strategic, product, and channel partnerships.

• Structure and negotiate the commercial terms and product setup for each partner.

• Build our new bank and credit union channel, landing the partners and integrations that make Figure easy for these institutions to adopt.

• Win partnerships in the home improvement and small business lending ecosystems that drive funded volume across multiple products (e.g. HELOC, fix-&-flip, DSCR).

• Coordinate the internal teams a launch depends on, including product, engineering, credit, legal, and implementation, to get partners live and scaling.

• Own each partnership internally. Spot where it is likely to stall and clear the path before it does.

• Build repeatable program structures and playbooks so each new partnership moves faster than the last.

• Track your deal pipeline and activity in Salesforce (our CRM).

What We Look For

• 5+ years in strategic partnerships, investment banking, venture capital / private equity, business development, consulting, or a related field (we care way more about your actual impact and scope of work than the exact years on your resume—so if you're a bit outside this range, definitely still apply!). Experience with lending, fintech, SaaS, or financial institutions is a plus.

• A track record building platform, product, or channel partnerships, ideally involving banks, credit unions, and non-bank lenders – including the systems they run on.

• Strong negotiation skills and the patience to run a long, multi-party process all the way to launch.

• A working understanding of consumer and small-business lending. You do not need deep capital-markets expertise for this role, but you should understand how originations work.

• Organized and detail-oriented, and good at getting cross-functional teams to move.

• Comfortable with ambiguity and able to own outcomes.

• Nice to have: experience partnering with or selling into depositories, POS, LOS, or core integrations, or home-improvement and small-business lending.

• Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures.

• Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes.

• Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team.

Salary

• Base Compensation Range: $120,000 - $150,000/yr

• On-target earnings: $190,000 - $240,000/yr

• Company equity in the form of RSUs

This is the compensation range for the role in the United States. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, internal equity, and evolving business needs. While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

Benefits

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employees and their dependents on select plans

• Company HSA, FSA, Dependent Care FSA, 401(k), and commuter benefits

• Employer-paid life and disability insurance

• 11 observed holidays and PTO plan

• Up to 12 weeks of paid family leave

• Continuing education reimbursement

California Residents, please review our California Employee and General Workforce Privacy Notice for further information. By submitting your application, you are agreeing and acknowledging that you have read and understand the above notice.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Cloud Availability
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About This Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own program execution for cloud availability — the maintenance windows, host patching, network switch upgrades, and incident management work that keeps our GPU infrastructure running reliably for customers. This role sits with an engineering team that manages system uptime and infrastructure SLAs and has not historically worked with a TPM function, so the right candidate earns credibility through technical depth and execution rigor rather than process alone. You'll drive planning and execution of maintenance windows that balance minimal customer disruption against critical hardware and firmware updates, coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents, and build the lightweight frameworks that bring predictability to an operationally complex environment. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to be personally in the room for incident calls and switch upgrade planning, not managing from a dashboard



What You’ll Be Working On:

 - Maintenance Window Planning & Execution: Own the planning and execution of maintenance windows/production changes for high-availability cloud infrastructure, balancing minimal customer workload disruption against the need for host patching and hardware updates.

 - Incident Management: Coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents or unplanned outages — driving communications, leading post-incident reviews (PIRs), and tracking remediation items through to closure without compromising SLA commitments.

 - Network Switch Upgrades: Support planning for major network switch upgrades and migrations, tracking the hardest dependencies and flagging what's most likely to break before it does.

 - Technical Risk Identification: Catch technical risks in cloud availability programs before the engineering team surfaces them, and know when to solve it directly versus escalate.

 - Vendor & Partner Coordination: Engage directly with hardware/network vendors and Customer Success on high-stakes infrastructure upgrades, keeping customer-facing teams informed through the process.

 - Program Frameworks: Build lightweight, fit-for-purpose execution frameworks for well-scoped availability and reliability programs (e.g., firmware update campaigns) where none exist today.

 - AI-Driven Program Execution: Actively use AI tools to improve risk identification, dependency tracking, and status communication in daily program work.

 - Engineering Credibility: Build trust with an engineering team that hasn't previously worked with a TPM — through technical fluency in maintenance workflows and incident processes, not through imposed process

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 2 to 5+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager, with direct exposure to cloud infrastructure, availability, or operations environments.

 - Working knowledge of maintenance window planning, host patching, and hardware/firmware update cycles for high-availability systems.

 - Experience with incident management practices: cross-functional incident coordination, post-incident reviews, and remediation tracking against SLA commitments.

 - Familiarity with network switch upgrade or migration planning, including how to identify and track critical dependencies.

 - Demonstrated ability to build basic, lightweight program processes for well-defined initiatives and to know when to escalate versus solve directly.

 - Active use of AI tools in program management work (risk detection, status reporting, dependency mapping), with concrete examples.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating incident response and reporting status across technical and customer-facing stakeholders

Bonus Points:

 - Direct experience in GPU or accelerated-computing cloud infrastructure environments.

 - Prior experience partnering with Customer Success or customer-facing teams during infrastructure upgrades.

 - Exposure to designing incident management or maintenance window frameworks from scratch, rather than operating within an existing one.

 - Experience navigating pushback from senior technical leaders without formal authority.




Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $200,000-$240,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Senior Application Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About Figure

Figure Technology Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: FIGR; OPEN: FGRS) is the leading blockchain-native capital marketplace for the origination, funding, sale, and trading of tokenized assets. More than 480 partners use its loan origination system and capital marketplace. Collectively, Figure and its partners have originated over $30 billion of loans to date, among other products. The fastest growing components are Figure Connect, its credit marketplace, and Democratized Prime, Figure’s on-chain lend-borrow marketplace. Figure’s ecosystem also includes DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) for asset custody and lien perfection, and $YLDS, a yield-bearing stablecoin registered with the SEC as a security under the Securities Act of 1933.

Figure is the market leader in real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. The company has received triple-A ratings from S&P and Moody’s on multiple loan securitizations, the first of its kind for blockchain finance.

We’re proud to be recognized as one of Forbes’ Top 50 Fintech Companies and CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies.

About the Role

As a Senior Application Security Engineer at Figure, you will be pivotal in the security of our software from the first line of code through deployment. You'll own and set the direction for our application security program, build and scale our vulnerability management program, embed secure coding practices into engineering workflows, and help ensure security standards are met at every stage of the software development lifecycle. We’re looking for a collaborative, hands-on senior engineer with a strong background in reading and writing code. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, DevOps, and IT to ensure our security processes are resilient, scalable, and seamlessly integrated into our workflows.

What You’ll Do

• Own and evolve Figure's vulnerability management program, including triage, prioritization, tracking remediation, and reporting on risk reduction over time.

• Collaborate with DevOps to integrate security gates at various points throughout the software development lifecycle, ensuring automation and repeatability of secure deployments.

• Manage third-party penetration tests, including scoping, vendor coordination, and tracking remediation of findings.

• Automate sources of toil, such as routine patching or dependency upgrades.

• Lead threat modeling, architecture reviews, and security design reviews for new features and services, partnering with engineering teams early in the design process.

• Lead cross-team initiatives that significantly improve our security posture while balancing speed and innovation.

• Define and drive Figure's application security strategy and roadmap, including secure coding standards and security requirements for new services.

• Mentor engineers across the organization and build a security champions program that scales secure development practices.

• Evaluate, select, and own application security tooling and vendors.

• Track program metrics and communicate application security risk to engineering and executive leadership.

• Actively participate in incident response, on-call rotations, and post-incident reviews to continuously improve defenses.

• Leverage AI to augment threat hunting, vulnerability scanning, and triage, using it to surface signal faster and reduce manual review load.

• Design and build AI agents to perform in-depth testing and analysis of our infrastructure and code.

What We Look For

• 6-8+ years in application security, product security, or a security-focused software engineering role.

• Strong coding ability in one or more languages used in modern web/backend development (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Java/Kotlin) — enough to read unfamiliar code, build tooling and automation, and propose concrete fixes, not just file findings.

• Hands-on experience building or scaling a vulnerability management program, including triage, prioritization, and remediation workflows.

• Experience integrating security tooling into CI/CD (SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets scanning, IaC scanning) and tuning it for signal over noise.

• Familiarity with software supply-chain security and dependency vetting (e.g., SCA platforms, tools like Semgrep, Snyk, Socket, or comparable).

• Deep knowledge of the OWASP Top 10, secure coding patterns, and common vulnerability classes, with the ability to teach them to other engineers.

• Extensive experience leading threat modeling and security design reviews.

• Strong cross-functional collaboration skills and the ability to drive remediation across teams without owning the code yourself.

• Track record of leading application security initiatives end to end, from strategy and roadmap through rollout and measurable results.

• Experience mentoring engineers and acting as a technical leader, including running or growing a security champions program.

• Ability to communicate risk and tradeoffs clearly to both engineers and leadership.

• Deep expertise in at least one area, such as authentication and authorization, cryptography, API security, or cloud-native application security.

• Relentless curiosity and persistence in investigating root causes and driving long-lasting improvements.

• Cloud security exposure (GCP a plus) and prior blockchain/Web3 security experience are pluses, not requirements.

• Familiarity with security and compliance requirements in regulated financial services (e.g., SOC 2, PCI DSS, GLBA) is a plus.

• Hands-on proficiency with AI-assisted security tooling and a practical sense of its strengths and limits.

• Adhere to all company security policies and data handling procedures.

• Complete mandatory security awareness training within required timeframes.

• Promptly report any suspected security incidents or suspicious activity to the Security team.

Salary

• Base Compensation Range: $112,320 - $168,480/yr

• 25% annual bonus target, paid quarterly

• Company equity in the form of RSUs

This is the compensation range for the role in the United States. Actual compensation may vary based on a candidate’s experience, skills, location, internal equity, and evolving business needs. While most offers are generally made within the middle of the range, final compensation is determined based on the factors above.

Benefits

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% employer-paid premiums for employees and their dependents on select plans

• Company HSA, FSA, Dependent Care FSA, 401(k), and commuter benefits

• Employer-paid life and disability insurance

• 11 observed holidays and PTO plan

• Up to 12 weeks of paid family leave

• Continuing education reimbursement

Depending on your residential location certain laws might regulate the way Figure manages applicant data. California Residents, please review our California Employee and General Workforce Privacy Notice for further information. By submitting your application, you are agreeing and acknowledging that you have read and understand the above notice.

Figure will not sponsor work visas for this position. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

 - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

 - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

 - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description:
ABOUT CLARIFY

Clarify is building the AI-native CRM — a platform designed from the ground up for how modern go-to-market teams actually work. We raised $22.5M and assembled a team of ~27 people who believe the CRM category is overdue for a complete rethink: less manual data entry, smarter automation, and AI that actually understands your pipeline.

We're early and moving fast. The work you do here will directly shape how we grow.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Clarify has shipped a lot in a short time: our AI Rep, permissions, reporting, and integrations with HubSpot, Stripe and Salesforce, with Signals launching in December. What we don't have yet is a product leader whose whole job is deciding what we build next, for whom, and making sure it lands. Today the founders do that alongside everything else.

You'll be Clarify's first Head of Product, reporting to our CEO. You'll set the product direction with our founders: who we build for, where we win and what we say no to. You'll own the roadmap, set the planning rhythm with engineering and design, and build a product team that great people want to join. At our stage this is a hands-on leadership role: you'll still talk to customers every week, write the specs that matter and prototype with AI yourself. You'll be accountable for whether what we ship gets used and moves retention and revenue.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Set product strategy and own the roadmap with our CEO and CTO, making the tradeoffs explicit

 - Build the product operating cadence with engineering squads and design: clear problems, tight scope, owners, dates and shipped outcomes

 - Own Tier 1 launches like Signals from scope to adoption, on the date we committed to

 - Own our core product metrics — weekly active usage and retention — and hold the roadmap accountable to them

 - Hire and lead the product team, starting with our first PMs, and partner closely with design

 - Stay hands-on: talk to customers every week and prototype ideas with AI before engineering commits time

 - Make the case for where product is going, in writing, to the team and to the board




YOUR BACKGROUND

 - You've led product at a B2B SaaS company at the Sr Director or VP level, running multiple PM teams, ideally as an early product leader through the Series A-C stage

 - You've hired, coached and led PMs, and people from your past teams would follow you to your next company

 - You've shipped 0-to-1 products customers rely on and can point to the metrics you moved

 - You've set a product direction and brought founders, engineering and go-to-market along with it

 - You're technical enough to go deep with engineers and direct AI-assisted prototyping; many great candidates started as engineers

 - You use AI natively in how you research, analyze and build

 - You know what process to add at our stage and what to skip, and you're still happy to do the work yourself

 - Bonus: You've built sales, CRM or GTM tools

 - Bonus: You've been a founder or a founding PM




COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

We offer a base salary range of $225,000-$275,000 depending on level and location, benchmarked against market data for startups our size, plus competitive stock options with standard 4-year vesting and a 1-year cliff. Benefits include fully covered medical, dental, and vision for you (50% for dependents), a 401(k) with company match, flexible time off, and generous parental leave. We bring the full team together 2–3 times a year for offsites.

Our Seattle-based employees work from our Pioneer Square office three days a week. Outside of Seattle, we're a fully distributed team.

Clarify is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to building an inclusive team and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

We operate like a startup, and encourage all of our employees to collaborate and voice feedback about our product and ways we can improve as a business. We believe in never settling, and that also pertains to your growth.

About the Role

The Head of Marketing will lead Skillz’s Growth and LiveOps, shaping how we attract, engage, retain, and grow the value of players across our platform. This is a broad leadership role spanning performance marketing, organic growth, lifecycle, LiveOps, and player offers and incentives.

We’re looking for a data-driven growth leader who understands both acquisition and the in-product player economy, has built and led high-performing teams, and knows how to turn customer insights and experimentation into sustainable growth. You’ll work closely with Product, Analytics, Engineering, Finance, and other leaders to help define and deliver the next phase of growth for Skillz.

Responsibilities

• Own both the Growth org and the LiveOps org for Skillz Platform — a single accountable owner for demand generation and for the in-app economy of events, offers and messaging that converts it.

• Lead Performance Marketing / UA (via the Head of Performance), Organic (ASO/CPP), and Creative — allocating spend across networks × games × surfaces against CAC-to-stable and stable-LTV, never CPI alone.

• Own the LiveOps operating model: per-game events, promos and offer slates across Solitaire Skillz, Blackout Bingo, Dominoes Gold and Arena, with a dedicated owner per surface.

jobs.title: Director, Nuclear Instrumentation & Electronics
jobs.description:
About Valar Atomics

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

You will lead a new product organization within Valar Atomics' Instrumentation, Control & Electrical (IC&E) organization, supplying hardware to the Reactor program across development, demonstration, and serial production units. The team you build will span detector design, analog and digital electronics, firmware, qualification and test, production engineering, and manufacturing operations. You will work alongside reactor I&C, automation and controls, reactor physics, nuclear safety, quality, supply chain, and licensing teams in a hands-on environment where measurement integrity directly supports reactor safety and production throughput. The team values technical depth, disciplined documentation, and a safety-first culture.

The Role

Valar Atomics is seeking Directors of Nuclear Instrumentation & Electronics to build and lead the organization that designs, qualifies, and manufactures the nuclear instrumentation and electronics required to scale reactor production. The role owns the full product lifecycle for neutron detectors, radiation monitors, signal processing electronics, and associated nuclear-grade hardware, from detector physics and circuit design through qualification, production engineering, manufacturing, and field support. The nuclear instrumentation supply base is thin, slow, and not built for serial reactor deployment; this role exists to make it an in-house capability that ships qualified hardware at production volume, on schedule, to nuclear quality standards.

Key Responsibilities

• Build and lead the Nuclear Instrumentation & Electronics organization, including hiring, organizational design, and development of engineering, test, and manufacturing teams; set technical standards and a culture of ownership and execution.

• Define and own the product roadmap for nuclear instrumentation and electronics, including make-versus-buy decisions, platform strategy, and cost, volume, and schedule targets aligned to the reactor production ramp.

• Own design of neutron flux detection hardware across source, intermediate, and power ranges, including fission chambers, ion chambers, proportional counters, and in-core or high-temperature detectors suited to the HTGR environment.

• Own design of radiation monitoring instrumentation, including area, process, and effluent monitors and associated detector assemblies.

• Own design of nuclear signal processing electronics, including high-voltage bias supplies, preamplifiers, pulse, current, and Campbell mode processing, digital pulse processing, FPGA and embedded firmware, and interfaces to protection and control systems.

• Lead equipment qualification programs, including environmental qualification (IEEE 323), seismic qualification (IEEE 344), EMI/RFI compatibility (Reg Guide 1.180), radiation and thermal aging, and qualification test planning, execution, and reporting.

• Ensure designs meet applicable nuclear safety system requirements, including IEEE 603, IEEE 7-4.3.2 for digital content, and software/firmware lifecycle and V&V requirements, in coordination with reactor I&C and licensing teams.

• Stand up and scale manufacturing operations for detectors and electronics, including production line design, assembly processes, cleanroom and contamination-controlled work areas, test fixtures and automated test equipment, yield management, and capacity planning.

• Drive design for manufacturability, test, and cost; transition designs from prototype to low-rate initial production to serial production with controlled production documentation.

• Establish and maintain the nuclear quality program for the product line, including 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and NQA-1 compliance, 10 CFR Part 21 reporting, commercial grade dedication of components, configuration management, and supplier qualification.

• Oversee licensing and material control requirements for detector production, including special nuclear material and byproduct material licensing (10 CFR Parts 30 and 70) for fissile coatings, neutron-sensitive materials, and calibration sources, in coordination with health physics and licensing teams.

• Own supply chain strategy for critical components and materials, including enriched uranium and boron-10 coatings, high-temperature ceramics and cabling, radiation-tolerant electronic components, and long-lead parts; develop second sources and manage obsolescence.

• Support NRC and DOE regulatory interactions for instrumentation design and qualification, including technical reports, audits, and responses to requests for additional information.

• Provide field support for installed hardware, including commissioning support, failure analysis, corrective action, and reliability data collection feeding back into design and manufacturing.

• Own organizational budget, headcount plan, and capital equipment plan for engineering, test, and manufacturing facilities.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Engineering Physics, or a related discipline.

• 12+ years of experience in radiation detection, nuclear instrumentation, or high-reliability electronics design and manufacturing, including 5+ years leading engineering or product teams.

• Deep technical knowledge of radiation detection physics and detector design, including neutron detection, gamma discrimination, and detector behavior in high-radiation and high-temperature environments.

• Hands-on background in analog and mixed-signal electronics for low-level signal measurement, including noise, grounding, shielding, and signal integrity in long cable runs.

• Demonstrated experience taking hardware products from design through qualification and into production, including DFM/DFT, production test, and yield improvement.

• Experience operating under a formal quality program in nuclear, aerospace, defense, medical device, or a comparably regulated industry.

• Working knowledge of nuclear equipment qualification and safety system standards, including IEEE 323, IEEE 344, IEEE 603, and Reg Guide 1.180.

• Proven ability to build teams from the ground up, hire and develop strong engineers, and deliver on aggressive schedules.

• This role requires access to technology controlled under U.S. export control regulations, including 10 CFR Part 810; candidates must be eligible to access such technology.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Master's or PhD in Nuclear Engineering, Physics, or Electrical Engineering with a focus on radiation detection or instrumentation.

• Professional Engineer (PE) license or eligibility.

• Direct experience designing or manufacturing fission chambers, ion chambers, self-powered neutron detectors, or radiation monitors at a nuclear instrumentation vendor, national laboratory, or reactor developer.

• Experience with nuclear safety-related hardware development under 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and NQA-1, including commercial grade dedication and 10 CFR Part 21 programs.

• Experience with FPGA-based or digital signal processing for nuclear instrumentation, including firmware V&V for safety-related applications.

• Experience with NRC or Agreement State materials licensing for special nuclear material or byproduct material.

• Experience scaling hardware manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment, including standing up new production facilities.

• Familiarity with HTGR or other advanced reactor instrumentation challenges, including high-temperature, helium-environment, and graphite-moderated core applications.

• Experience with electronics manufacturing standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001) and radiation-tolerant component selection.

What We Offer

• Competitive base salary

• Equity ownership in a rapidly growing advanced energy company

• Comprehensive medical benefits

• Unlimited PTO

• Free daily lunch and dinner provided onsite

• Generous PPE stipend

• High-impact startup environment with significant ownership and autonomy

• Opportunities for rapid career growth and internal advancement

• Direct collaboration with experienced operators, engineers, and industry leaders

• The opportunity to help build and scale transformative energy technology from the ground up

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Valar Atomics is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status under applicable law.

We are committed to providing a workplace free of discrimination and harassment and will provide reasonable accommodation as required by law.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident (green card holder).

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, GenAI Platform
jobs.description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

About the role:

Foundation AI builds the platforms, services, and infrastructure that enable machine learning and generative AI across Roblox. As a Principal Engineer on this team, you'll set technical strategy and direction across areas such as model training and inference, LLM services, agent infrastructure, data systems, experimentation, evaluation, and developer tooling. You'll be accountable for the architecture and long-term health of systems that many teams depend on, and you'll shape how Roblox builds AI — partnering with engineering, product, research, data, infrastructure, safety, creator, engine, discovery, and economy. You will report to an Engineering Manager within the Foundation AI organization.

You will:

• Define the multi-year technical vision and architecture for platforms and services that power machine learning, generative AI, and agentic experiences across Roblox.

• Drive the hardest, most ambiguous, highest-leverage problems on the platform from framing through production on multi-provider inference resiliency and scaling information retrieval infrastructure for agentic use and be accountable for the outcomes.

• Establish the standards, paved paths, and guardrails that make the platform self-serve for every team at Roblox — multi-tenant usage attribution and metering, built-in spend controls, and fast, ticket-free onboarding.

• Make foundational trade-offs in quality, latency, reliability, cost, and responsible data use for systems operating at Roblox scale — treating instrumentation and observability as a first principle of the architecture, not an afterthought.

• Own the operational standard for the platform at scale — SLOs, capacity planning, on-call, and incident response and design for graceful degradation and fast recovery, not just steady-state correctness.

• Identify high-impact opportunities and risks ahead, and build alignment across engineering and leadership to act on them.

• Multiply the impact of other engineers through technical mentorship, design and code review, and setting the bar for engineering excellence.

You have:

• An undergraduate/graduate degree in computer science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• 8+ years of experience building and operating large-scale production software, distributed systems, cloud services, or related infrastructure.

• A sustained track record of designing and owning foundational systems or platforms with organization- or company-wide impact.

• Deep expertise in one or more of machine learning, generative AI, distributed systems, data infrastructure, or developer platforms, with the breadth to reason across all of them.

• Expert proficiency in one or more of Go, Python, or Rust, and the judgment to choose the right tools for durable systems.

• A history of setting technical direction across multiple teams and driving large, cross-organizational efforts to completion.

• Exceptional communication and influence skills, with the ability to align engineers, product, and leadership around a technical strategy.

Nice to have:

• Experience building or operating an LLM gateway, inference-serving, or model-routing layer — multi-provider failover, rate limiting, and token/cost accounting at scale.

• Hands-on work with vector databases, similarity search, or knowledge graphs, and with RAG or agentic systems (retrieval pipelines, agent memory, context management, evaluating non-deterministic systems).

• Experience designing multi-tenant platforms — usage attribution, metering, spend controls, and self-serve onboarding.

• Background in GPU infrastructure or ML inference efficiency (batching, quantization, accelerator utilization, cost optimization).

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description:
GoodParty.org is looking for a growth and user-obsessed Staff Product Manager to turn running as an Independent from a long shot into a real path to office. You'll own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap behind the tools tens of thousands of candidates and elected officials use to put people over parties.

You'll partner closely with our CPO, Design, and Engineering teams to turn ideas into scalable solutions and build the funnels that drive adoption and growth. The ideal candidate has an 8+ year track record of taking products from 0 to 1 and beyond, with the instincts to know when to pivot and the discipline to let data prove it.

About GoodParty.org:

A majority of voters, including more than half of Millennials and Gen Z, say that neither major party represents them. GoodParty.org is the solution.

We're on a mission to make people matter more than money in our democracy by empowering Independent candidates to run, win, and serve.

Since 2024, 13,000+ Independent candidates have won their races across all 50 states using our tools, training, and support. Our AI-powered platform provides free tools to launch and run campaigns, connect with voters, and serve their communities effectively — without needing a political party or big donors. What our users have in common is that they prioritize people over parties and community over special interests. We're not a political party, we're a platform and a movement to democratize democracy.

Founded by serial entrepreneur Farhad Mohit ($1B+ in exits, including Flipagram/TikTok and Shopzilla), GoodParty.org is building solutions so we can have a truly representative democracy where society's biggest problems are solved.

What you’ll do:

 - Drive the  product vision, strategy, and roadmap in collaboration with the product team and politics team stakeholders.

 - Turn ideas into scalable product solutions that empower independents to explore a run for office, run winning campaigns, and serve in office.

 - Leverage your passion for users to organize user research and testing across our politically diverse user base in collaboration with the design team.

 - Productize emerging AI tools to improve our products and features and scale yourself.

 - Create cohesive funnels that drive user adoption, growth, and unlock a viable path for independent candidates.

 - Apply quantitative and qualitative methods to validate ideas, learn from user interactions or feedback, and improve metrics on existing products.

 - Report to the CPO and partner closely with our Designer and Engineering team.

Who we’re looking for:

 - You’re up for the audacious challenge of transforming our democracy by making running as an independent a viable path to getting elected into service. You’re very curious about this problem space or are already passionate about it.

 - You thrive in a remote, fast-paced environment, balancing strategic thinking with a strong bias toward action.

 - You’re a proven A-player with a 8+ year track record of building tech products, with increasing responsibility and success.

 - You’ve either built something from scratch or were very early on a product that went from 0 or 0.5 to 1 (and beyond). You’re quick to pivot when the need arises or a better path emerges.

 - You get obsessed with your user. You research them and proactively try to make them as successful as possible by improving the product.

 - You’re analytical with a metrics mindset, plus you’ve got the data, optimization, and problem solving skills to ensure products meet their potential.

 - You’re actively using emerging AI tools and understand the basics of prompt engineering both to scale yourself and improve products and features.

 - You have a baseline understanding of how the American political system works.

 - You’re able to work independently and also enjoy collaborating with others to iteratively solve problems in real-time. You thrive working at the startup speed that our mission demands.

 - You pursue understanding user perspectives and behavior with curiosity and empathy.

 - You communicate clearly, directly, and respectfully, and you're open to delivering and receiving candid feedback that helps the team grow.

Bonus if:

 - You have experience working in small, tight-knit, fast-paced remote teams.

 - You have professional or volunteer experience in civic tech, democracy reform, political campaigns, or social impact initiatives.

 - You're tired of sitting on the sidelines while democracy fails to meet its potential — and you're ready to act.

Why you should work at GoodParty.org:

 - Join a passionate team with diverse political views focused on one mission. Our values are: People First. Direct, Open, and Honest. Empowered Ownership. Iterate for Impact. Fun Is Fuel.

 - We're a Public Benefit Corporation that prioritizes social impact over profit.

 - Innovative Bitcoin denominated deferred bonus plan, allowing you to have the amazing upside of being in a startup while working on a truly meaningful mission.

 - Work where and how you like, on a fully remote team spread across the country.

 - 100% coverage of health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents.

 - We encourage you to take time off to recharge and have an unlimited PTO (sick and vacation) policy. This is a marathon, not a sprint. We believe a work-life balance is needed to get there.

 - 401(k) program available so you can contribute toward retirement savings (no employer match).

 - Individual learning & development budget to fund your growth.

 - We'll make sure you've got what you need to work remotely through our workspace setup stipend.

 - If you work from home, we give $50/month to help with your internet and other expenses. If you prefer co-working, that's an option we can discuss too.

 - Fully funded for our mission. No stressing over whether the next round of funding will come through. Focus on making an impact. That's what matters here.

The salary range is $184,000 - 200,000 for this remote, full-time position with excellent benefits. This range reflects the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. An employee's position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, seniority, education, qualifications, certifications, and organizational needs. We reserve the right to modify this pay range at any time.

We are not considering candidates currently based outside of the US, so please only apply if you are physically located in the US. Unfortunately, we are not able to provide sponsorship for any of our roles at this time.

Ready to learn more or apply?

We hope you'll apply! You can also keep up with the latest by signing up at GoodParty.org/about http://GoodParty.org/about. If you know anyone else who may be interested, please share this job posting — thanks!

jobs.title: Manager, Solutions Architecture Transformation
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) Transformation team makes focused global investments that turn SA strategy and innovation into scalable capabilities—elevating technical excellence and compounding impact for SAs, users, and Stripe. We partner with global SA leadership, GTM, Product, and Engineering to bring strategy to life, develop better ways for SAs to work, and scale promising innovation from the field. We combine field and user insight, disciplined experimentation, and emerging technology to build durable capabilities that raise the bar for the global SA organization.

The team combines transformation program leadership with close, matrixed partnerships across AI Engineering and Demo Engineering. This leader will directly manage the team’s program-management leader and bring these groups together around shared priorities, clear operating mechanisms, and measurable outcomes.

What you’ll do

As Manager of SA Transformation, you will set the vision, priorities, and operating model for a high-impact team responsible for turning strategy and innovation into durable, globally scalable capabilities. You will lead a group of program managers, and be second line leader to the leader for the AI Engineers, and Demo Engineers. You’ll coach the team through ambiguous, cross-functional work while staying close to the highest-leverage initiatives—from early signal and experimentation through launch, adoption, and long-term ownership. You will be a key strategic partner to SA leadership and leaders across GTM, Product, and Engineering, ensuring the transformation portfolio materially improves how SAs work and the outcomes they deliver for users.

Responsibilities

• Set the strategy, priorities, and operating model for the SA Transformation team, translating SA, GTM, and Product direction into a focused portfolio of capabilities, experiments, and programs

• Manage and develop the team, empowering them to lead day-to-day program execution while setting clear expectations, providing coaching, and building the organization’s long-term capabilities

• Create an inclusive, high-performing team environment grounded in accountability, strong judgment, and a shared commitment to user impact

• Identify recurring friction in SA workflows and design better tools, practices, and operating models that improve effectiveness and technical excellence across regions, segments, and motions

• Build strong interlocks with Product, Product Operations, Product Marketing, Field Marketing, Developer Relations, Enablement, and Operations so field insight informs strategy and promising ideas can earn global scale

• Establish shared priorities and operating mechanisms across Transformation Programs, AI Engineering, and Demo Engineering, partnering with technical leaders and SA innovators to build and scale tools, demos, and automated workflows that measurably improve SA productivity and user outcomes

Who you are

Minimum requirements

• 10+ years of experience in go-to-market program management, business operations, management consulting, or a related discipline

• 3+ years of experience directly managing and developing high-performing teams in program management, strategy, operations, product, engineering, or a comparable discipline, including experience managing through another people leader and maintaining accountability without taking over day-to-day execution

• Track record of building high-performing teams through clear expectations, coaching, thoughtful work allocation, and performance management

• Experience setting a team or portfolio strategy and translating broad organizational priorities into focused, measurable programs

• End-to-end global delivery expertise in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, with a strong ability to solve complex commercial, operational, and workflow challenges

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, adept at analyzing data, influencing across levels (IC to C-Suite), and aligning cross-functional teams around common objectives

• Experience identifying, evaluating, and scaling AI or automation opportunities that produce measurable workflow or productivity improvements beyond basic prompt engineering

Preferred qualifications

• Leadership experience in Solutions Architecture, Solutions Engineering, or a technical GTM transformation function

• Domain expertise in fintech, financial services, payments, or regulated technology environments

• Track record of scaling global GTM functions across AMER, EMEA, and APAC during periods of rapid growth

• Experience taking ideas from field signal through experimentation, launch, adoption, and a durable long-term operating model

Credentialed Veterinary Technician (LVT/CVT/RVT)

$25 - $36 per hour | Up to $2,000 Sign-On Bonus | Flexible Schedules
